jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Parking Garage Bounty
jokes.joke: I'd be a terrible bounty hunter. The whole profession is based on finding people, and I once got lost looking for my own car in a parking garage. After forty minutes I found a guy wandering between the rows and thought, “Finally, the fugitive.” Nope—he'd lost his Honda too. We teamed up. Technically, we both brought someone in.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Wrong Turn
jokes.joke: My husband refuses to ask for directions. Says he's never lost, he's just exploring. Forty minutes into exploring a farm road, I suggested we ask someone. He said, 'Ask who? There's nobody out here.' Then I got out my phone, and he said, 'Don't you dare use a map. That's cheating.' Sir, you're the only man who's ever gotten lost with a GPS and still blamed the satellite for being too far away.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Safety First
jokes.joke: Bounty hunters are massive hypocrites. A guy will kick your door off the hinges, taser you in the living room, zip-tie your wrists, and toss you into the back of a Dodge Caravan. But the minute you sit up, he checks the rearview and goes, 'Hey, buckle up, I'm not getting a ticket.' My mistake, man. I didn't realize we were prioritizing traffic safety during a kidnapping.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Wrong Turn Bounty
jokes.joke: I signed up to be a bounty hunter thinking it’d be all high-stakes chases. First job, track this guy through the woods. Two days later I’m completely stranded, walking in circles with no signal and half a protein bar. When I finally stumble onto his camp, he’s just sitting there roasting marshmallows. Looks up and says, “Took you long enough. Want one?”

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Excellent Navigation
jokes.joke: I got stranded on a lake with a guy who kept introducing himself as a sea captain. After three hours of drifting in circles, I asked, "Are you sure you're a captain?" He said, "Absolutely. Getting somewhere is the crew's department."

scores.comment: Clear and stage-ready, but the direction-refusal premise is very familiar; the satellite line gives it a decent extra tag.
Strong contrast between violent apprehension and fussy traffic safety; clean escalation and a solid final line.
Readable and well-structured, with a nice role reversal, but the marshmallow payoff is more charming than sharply funny.
Very economical setup and a crisp character-revealing punchline; amusing and polished without quite reaching an 8-level laugh.
Strong self-deprecating premise with a real turn: the 'fugitive' is just another lost person. The last line ('we both brought someone in') lands cleanly, though it's slightly explained.

Good specific escalation (door, taser, zip-ties, Caravan) into a fresh image of a kidnapper who cares about seatbelt tickets. The closing line slightly explains the joke, but the hypocrisy angle is clear and well built.
Pleasant, clean story with a mild payoff in the relaxed fugitive offering a marshmallow. The turn is gentle and somewhat predictable, and it reads more like an anecdote than a punchline.
Compact and understandable, and 'getting somewhere is the crew's department' is a decent line. The premise is thin, with little build-up, and the turn is fairly easy to see coming.
Nice structural turn combining the target and the hunter as lost partners, though the premise is slightly familiar.
Relies heavily on one of the oldest comedy tropes (husbands not asking for directions), resulting in a predictable and clunky punchline.
Plays out more like a mild movie scene than a punchy stand-up bit; the ending is competent but lacks a strong comedic snap.
A clean, nicely constructed street-style joke that works fairly well as an onstage anecdote with a solid logic-reversal punchline.
Solid premise and clean closer, but the parking-garage lost-car setup is familiar and the payoff stays mild.
Classic husband-directions trope with a stretched satellite punch; recognizable but forgettable.
Clear stage premise, sharp hypocrisy turn, and a final line that lands the laugh cleanly.
Concise and on-premise, but thin escalation and a mild punch that doesn’t fully carry.
Clear premise and callback; teaming up with another lost person is a decent turn, though the final line is more clever than laugh-out-loud.
Relatable lost-driver premise, but the GPS/satellite punchline follows a familiar path and lacks a strong snap.
Strong hypocrisy angle, vivid specifics, and a clean final contrast that carries the laugh.
Fun role-reversal image with the fugitive casually waiting, but the ending is gentle rather than a big punch.
